bull.b: Strong first-half revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA growth indicates improving operating scale and customer economics. Although higher gold prices helped, the margin expansion and earnings progress strengthen internal funding capacity and support the business over the next several quarters.

The How Mine expansion materially increases processing capacity and is expected to support an annualized production rate above 30,000 ounces. Once commissioned and ramped, this added throughput can improve operating scale and provide a clearer platform for 2027 production.

A 61% increase in operating cash flow demonstrates that the core business is generating more cash from operations, providing resources for mine development and restart activity. Reinvesting this cash can strengthen production capacity without relying solely on external capital.

bear.b: Persistently negative shareholder equity is a durable balance-sheet weakness that reduces financial flexibility and leaves less protection if operating conditions deteriorate. It can also constrain access to funding and make future investment or restructuring decisions more difficult.

The large working capital deficit and only $1.8 million of cash indicate significant near-term funding pressure relative to obligations. This reduces the company’s ability to absorb operational setbacks and increases reliance on cash generation, facilities, and disciplined capital deployment.

Reduced production guidance alongside higher expected all-in sustaining costs signals weaker near-term operating efficiency and less production leverage. Lower ounces spread fixed costs across a smaller base, potentially limiting cash generation and making the expansion ramp increasingly important.
